renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: orf_record
  title: ORF record
  description: |-
    The card shows every field of one Ribo-TISH ORF: its gene, transcript, location, initiation type, start codon, length and frame-test q-value. It answers what is known about the ORF picked in the table.
    How to read: select a row in the table to fill the card. A low frame-test q-value means the in-frame reads are significantly more numerous than the out-of-frame ones.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zhpn1024/ribotish/master/README.rst
  kind: record_card
  roles:
    id: orf_id
    title: gene_name

- component: card
  title: ORFs predicted
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct ORFs Ribo-TISH predicted, and the ring splits them by class (annotated coding sequence, N-terminal variant, upstream, downstream, internal or novel ORF). It answers how much translation beyond annotated starts the data supports.
    How to read: annotated coding sequences are the baseline. A large share of novel or upstream ORFs is the interesting part but needs follow-up, for example with a second caller.
  column: orf_id
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: orf_class
  caption: ORFs, by class

- component: card
  title: ORF length
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median ORF length in amino acids and the histogram shows the distribution. It answers whether the calls are full proteins or short ORFs.
    How to read: a histogram with a large short peak points to many small ORFs such as upstream ones. Filter by ORF class to separate them from annotated coding sequences.
  column: aa_length
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: lengths, in amino acids

- component: figure
  title: ORF length by class
  description: |-
    Each bar counts ORFs in a length bin, split by ORF class. It answers how the classes differ in length.
    How to read: annotated coding sequences spread over long lengths while small ORFs pile up on the left. A class with an unusual length profile, for example long novel ORFs, deserves a closer look in the table.
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: aa_length
    color: orf_class
    labels:
      aa_length: ORF length (amino acids)
      orf_class: ORF class

- component: interactive
  title: ORF class
  description: Restricts every tile to the chosen ORF classes, such as upstream or novel ORFs. It answers
    whether a pattern belongs to annotated genes or to the new calls.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: orf_class

- component: table
  title: Ribo-TISH ORFs
  description: |-
    Each row is an ORF in one library, collapsed from its start codons, with its gene, transcript, location, class, start codon, length and frame-test q-value. It answers which ORFs to follow up.
    How to read: sort by the q-value or the length and select a row to fill the ORF record.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: orf_id
